argument_summary: The supportable position on the current admissible record is narrower than a clean nondisclosure defense. Aggregate readiness is above threshold and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports launch readiness in general. Public governance guidance also supports certification with documented limitations and continued monitoring. But the same record shows the small-business onboarding segment is 1.3 points below target, is named in two paid pilot commitments, legal review is still open, and no approved risk acceptance or final resolution is in evidence. The defensible ask is therefore to treat the certification theory as caveated rather than escalatory misconduct: the record supports readiness plus an unresolved materiality question, not a proven satisfaction of the nondisclosure predicate.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost should not drive the policy conclusion. The relevant operational point is only that escalation is not necessary if the auditor can distinguish between unsupported clean compliance and a narrower, caveated certification posture tied to monitoring and explicit acknowledgment of the unresolved materiality issue.
claims_about_policy: On this record, policy compliance should be framed narrowly. The admissible evidence does not show that the limitation was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, so a clean finding that nondisclosure was policy-compliant is not supported. At the same time, aggregate-readiness evidence and public governance guidance are relevant to whether certification can be defended in a monitored, caveated posture. The proper policy characterization is an unresolved disclosure predicate attached to an otherwise supportable readiness showing.
concessions: No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering the small-business onboarding gap before launch.
No admissible evidence shows final legal resolution of whether the gap must be disclosed.
The affected segment is named in two paid pilot commitments, which keeps materiality live under the available policy text.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one incidents do not by themselves satisfy the release policy's disclosure predicate.
